text:
ana: FYI observed a cluster of WS clients that reconnect twice within ~200ms and then stop resuming. Happening on us-east at ~04:20. tagging eng-platform
devon: Logs show client initiated reconnect -> server closed with status 204 and no resume token exchange. Clients retry quickly, token expires, then they fall back to cold start.
rui: Is this tenant-scoped? We saw a similar pattern but with SSE last month.
nana: typo, meant 'ana' :)
ana: It's Tenant alpha-7. I grabbed the edge-proxy dump: several FIN+RST combos followed by `HTTP/1.1 204 No Content` logs from the graceful-close handler.
devon: Can you paste the handler snippet?
ana: ```
// graceful_close handler
if (idle_ms > ttl) {
  send_http_response(204, "");
  close_tcp();
}
```
rui: That 204 is being interpreted by our LB as an application-level response not an EOF for streaming lanes. So the client sees a 200-ish and re-opens but without resume handshake.
metrics-bot: metric spike: increase(streaming_reconnects_total{tenant="alpha-7"}[5m]) = 3200; increase(stream_resume_attempts_total{tenant="alpha-7"}[5m]) = 90; increase(stream_resume_success_total{tenant="alpha-7"}[5m]) = 10.
devon: Oof. That explains the duplicate billing and token churn. Resume attempts << reconnects.
nana: We rolled out `close_on_idle: true` via console for alpha-7 at 04:12 as part of cost-savings schedule.
console-bot: rollout-bot: console rollout "close-on-idle" tenant=alpha-7 started 04:11:58, target=100% complete 04:12:07.
rui: Proposed fixes: (1) Change close status to 499/499-like so proxies treat it as connection termination; (2) Keep 204 but add header `x-rw-stream-close: idle` and teach gateway to treat it as EOF; (3) Introduce server-side resume grace window where token TTL is extended by 30s after close.
nana: I prefer (2) + (3). Changing status codes could interact poorly with client libraries and infra rules. Header is explicit and safe.
devon: Agree on header. Need to update docs and console UI to warn about status semantics.
rui: Also add telemetry: `stream_close_code_total{code="204", reason="graceful_idle"}` and `stream_resume_window_extension_seconds` gauge when grace applied.
metrics-bot: example PromQL for dashboard: `sum by (tenant, code) (increase(stream_close_code_total[5m]))` and `sum(increase(streaming_reconnects_total[5m])) / max(1, sum(increase(stream_resume_success_total[5m])))` for reconnect/resume ratio.
nana: UX point: current dashboard stacks reconnects and resumes but doesn't show close codes. Users see weird ratios and file tickets. We should add a side panel for close_code breakdown.
devon: Short mitigation: revert console rollout for alpha-7 and roll back to previous handler. Then release header+telemetry change behind canary.
rui: I'll open ENG-3502 and add instrumentation PR. Include PromQL and alert: `increase(streaming_reconnects_total[1m]) > 5 * increase(stream_resume_success_total[1m])` with a suppression for tenant-level maintenance windows.
nana: I'll revert now and post status. If revert stabilizes in 5m, we proceed with header plan.
devon: Ping me when revert goes out so I can validate logs and connection state machine.
metrics-bot: revert event: console rollout rollback1 tenant=alpha-7 completed 04:24:11.
nana: Revert in. Early signs look better  reconnects dropping to baseline. Will keep observing for 10m then close ticket.
rui: Action items: rui -> ENG-3502 + metrics PR; devon -> implement header handling in gateway; ana -> revert confirm + postmortem draft; console -> add UI warning about close status semantics.
nana: thanks all :)
